266/72.plain: Fraudulently using, without authority, the name of a fraternity or similar organization in publications, soliciting members under it, or offering its degrees or work is punishable by up to 1 year of imprisonment, a $500 fine, or both.
acts: fraudulently uses or aids in any way in the use of the name, title or common designation of any fraternity, association, society, order, organization or union
fraudulently publishes, sells, circulates or distributes any written or printed letter, notice, matter or device, in any way soliciting members
fraudulently offers to sell, confer, communicate or give information where, of whom or by what means any degree or work

266/73.plain: Obtaining goods by falsely pretending to carry on a business in the ordinary course of trade, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: obtains from any person goods or chattels

266/74.plain: A corporate officer, agent, clerk or servant who wilfully uses the corporation's credit for personal benefit without authority, or fraudulently lends, appropriates or converts its money or property, faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: uses the name of such corporation, or his own name as such officer, agent, clerk or servant, to obtain money upon the credit of such corporation for his own use or benefit
fraudulently lends, invests or appropriates the money or disposes of the property of such corporation, or fraudulently converts it

266/75.plain: Fraudulently obtaining property by a game, sleight of hand, pretended fortune telling, or a trick with cards or other implements is punished the same as larceny of property of like value.
acts: fraudulently obtains from another person property of any description

266/75A.plain: Operating a vending machine, turnstile, coin telephone or similar coin receptacle with a slug or unauthorized trick, or taking goods or service from one without paying, is punishable by up to 30 days in a house of correction and a $100 fine.
acts: operates or causes to be operated, or attempts to operate or to cause to be operated, any automatic vending machine, slot machine, turnstile, coin-box telephone or other receptacle
takes, obtains or receives from or in connection with any automatic vending machine, slot machine, turnstile, coin-box telephone or other receptacle

266/75B.plain: Making, advertising, selling or giving away slugs or devices meant to cheat coin-operated machines, turnstiles or coin telephones is punishable by up to 1 year in a house of correction, a $500 fine, or both.
acts: manufactures for sale, advertises for sale, sells, offers for sale, or gives away any slug, device or substance whatsoever

266/75C.plain: Selling a gift certificate that expires in less than 7 years, or refusing to redeem a sold gift certificate before its expiration date, is punishable by a fine of up to $300.
acts: sells or offers to sell a gift certificate
refuses to redeem the certificate before it has reached the expiration date

266/75D.plain: Selling a gift certificate that carries dormancy, administrative, service or other fees reducing its redeemable value is punishable by a fine of up to $300 per violation.
acts: sells or offers to sell a gift certificate

266/75E.plain: Selling a gift certificate with fees or charges without printing notice of those fees on the certificate or its packaging is punishable by a fine of up to $300 per violation.
acts: sells or offers to sell a gift certificate
Failure to print such notice

266/75F.plain: Deducting a gratuity from a gift certificate when redeeming it, without the holder's consent, is punishable by a fine of up to $300 per violation.
acts: redeems a gift certificate, as defined in section 1 of chapter 255D and deducts a gratuity therefrom

266/76.plain: Committing any gross fraud or cheat at common law is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison, up to 2 years in jail, or a fine of up to $400.
acts: is convicted of any gross fraud or cheat at common law

266/77.plain: Making or selling articles marked "sterling" or "coin" silver that do not contain the required proportion of pure silver is punishable by a fine of up to $100.
acts: makes or sells, or offers to sell or dispose of, or has in his possession with intent so to do, any article of merchandise marked, stamped or branded

266/78.plain: Making or selling gold articles marked as finer than they are by more than one carat, or gold-filled or plated articles overstating their gold content by more than one percent, is punishable by a fine of up to $500.
acts: makes or sells, or offers for sale or disposes of, or has in his possession with intent so to do, any article constructed in whole or in part of gold or alloy of gold

266/79.plain: Selling, exchanging, or offering manufactured imitation furs while representing them as genuine fur of certain animals is punishable by a fine of $200 to $500.
acts: sells or exchanges, or has in his custody or possession with intent so to do, or exposes for sale or exchange, any manufactured imitations of furs of fur-bearing animals

266/80.plain: Conveying land known to be encumbered without telling the buyer about the encumbrance before payment is punishable by up to 1 year of imprisonment or a $1,000 fine.
acts: conveys land

266/81.plain: Selling and conveying one's land, knowing it is attached on mesne process, without notifying the grantee and with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison.
acts: sells and conveys it without giving notice of the attachment to the grantee

266/82.plain: Removing or concealing mortgaged personal property to put it beyond the mortgagee's control, or using rented, leased or mortgaged property to sell liquor illegally, is punishable by up to 1 year of imprisonment or a $1,000 fine.
acts: removes or conceals or aids or abets in removing or concealing the same
assents to such removal or concealment
use rented, leased or mortgaged personal property as a container or implement of sale of intoxicating liquor contrary to law

266/83.plain: A mortgagor who sells personal property without the mortgagee's written consent and without telling the buyer it is mortgaged faces up to 1 year of imprisonment or a $100 fine.
acts: sells or conveys the same or any part thereof without the written consent of the mortgagee

266/84.plain: A hirer or lessee who sells personal property without the owner's written consent and without telling the buyer it is hired or leased faces up to 1 year of imprisonment or a $100 fine.
acts: sells or conveys the same or any part thereof without the written consent of the owner or lessor

266/85.plain: Selling, pledging or otherwise disposing of collateral security before the debt is due, without the depositor's authority, is punishable by up to 2 years in jail or a $500 fine.
acts: sells, pledges, lends or in any way disposes of the same before such debt becomes due and payable

266/86.plain: Buying, receiving or helping conceal personal property known to be hired, leased or held as collateral, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to 1 year of imprisonment or a $100 fine.
acts: buys, receives or aids in concealing personal property

266/87.plain: A person renting or leasing personal property who conceals it, fails to return it within 10 days after the lease ends, or sells it without consent commits larceny of leased property, punishable by up to 1 year and restitution.
acts: conceals or aids or abets the concealment of such property or any part thereof
fails or refuses to return such property to the owner within ten days after expiration of the lease or rental agreement
sells, conveys or pledges such property or any part thereof without the written consent of the owner

266/87A.plain: Requires owners or lessees of stolen leased or rented motor vehicles to report the loss to police, and requires police to list and disseminate the information as for other stolen vehicles.

266/88.plain: A consignee or factor who, in bad faith and with intent to defraud the owner, pledges or converts consigned merchandise, instruments or their proceeds faces a $5,000 fine and up to 5 years of imprisonment.
acts: deposits or pledges, as security for money borrowed by him, a negotiable instrument received by him, merchandise consigned or intrusted to him, or a bill of lading, certificate or order for the delivery of merchandise
disposes of or applies such property or evidence of property to his own use
disposes of or applies to his own use money which has been raised or a negotiable instrument which has been acquired by the sale or other disposition of such property or evidence of property

266/89.plain: Falsely claiming in writing to hold a degree or to have been an officer or teacher of a school, or conferring degrees without authority, is punishable by up to 1 year and a $1,000 fine; misusing "university" or "college" brings a $1,000 fine.
acts: knowingly and falsely pretends to have been an officer or teacher, or to be a graduate or to hold any degree
offers or confers degrees as a school, college or as a private individual
using the designation of “university” or “college”

266/90.plain: Falsely and fraudulently claiming in writing the endorsement or approval of a college, university or professional school to promote a person, services or goods is punishable by up to 1 year, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: makes any false and fraudulent statement or assertion of endorsement, authority, approval or sanction of an incorporated college, university or professional school

266/91.plain: Publishing an advertisement to sell goods, securities or services that contains a statement the advertiser knew, or could reasonably have found, was untrue, deceptive or misleading is punishable by a fine of $1,000 to $2,000.
acts: makes, publishes, disseminates, circulates or places before the public, or causes, directly or indirectly, to be made, published, disseminated, circulated or placed before the public within the commonwealth

266/91A.plain: Advertising merchandise or services as part of a scheme not to sell them as advertised or at the stated price (bait advertising) is punishable by a fine of $500 to $1,000 or up to 1 year.
acts: offers for sale merchandise, commodities or service by making, publishing, disseminating, circulating or placing before the public within the commonwealth

266/91B.plain: Allows the attorney general or any aggrieved party to seek an injunction in superior court against advertising merchandise or services with intent not to sell them as advertised or at the stated price.

266/147.plain: Willfully making, using, advertising, selling, or possessing to sell goods or services bearing a counterfeit trademark is a crime; penalties rise with quantity, value and repeat offenses, up to 10 years in state prison plus fines.
acts: manufactures, uses, displays, advertises, distributes, offers for sale, sells or possesses with intent to sell or distribute any item or services bearing or identified by a counterfeit mark

266/148.plain: Sets duties for licensed dealers buying catalytic converters; enforced by civil fines and license sanctions, not as a crime.

266/1.plain: Wilfully and maliciously burning a dwelling house, or a building next to one or whose burning burns one, or helping do so, is punishable by up to 20 years in state prison.
acts: sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned
aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a dwelling house

266/2.plain: Wilfully and maliciously burning a church, public building, business building, vessel, vehicle, bridge, or other building or structure not a dwelling, or helping do so, is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: sets fire to, burns, or causes to be burned
aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a meeting house

266/5.plain: Wilfully and maliciously burning wood, lumber, crops, trees, fences, another's personal property worth over $25, or any boat or motor vehicle, or helping do so, is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison.
acts: sets fire to, or burns or otherwise destroys or injures by burning, or causes to be burned or otherwise so destroyed or injured
aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a pile or parcel of wood

266/5A.plain: Wilfully and maliciously attempting to burn any building, structure or property covered by the preceding arson sections, helping in the attempt, or doing any preliminary act, is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: attempts to set fire to, or attempts to burn
aids, counsels or assists in such an attempt to set fire to or burn
commits any act preliminary thereto or in furtherance thereof

266/7.plain: Wantonly or recklessly setting or increasing a fire that injures or destroys another's growing or standing wood is punishable by up to 2 years of imprisonment or a $1,000 fine.
acts: setting fire to any material, or by increasing a fire already set, causes injury to, or the destruction of, any growing or standing wood of another

266/8.plain: Setting or increasing a fire on another's land that injures another's property, or letting a fire on your own land spread and injure others' property, is punishable by up to 2 years of imprisonment or a $1,000 fine.
acts: sets or increases a fire upon land of another whereby the property of another is injured
suffers any fire upon his own land to extend beyond the limits thereof whereby the woods or property of another are injured

266/9.plain: In towns that accept it, failing to put out a fire you set on another's land, or wilfully or negligently setting or letting fires escape that endanger or injure property, is punishable by up to 1 month in jail and a $100 fine.
acts: sets a fire on land which is not owned or controlled by him and before leaving the same neglects to entirely extinguish such fire
sets a fire on land which is not owned or controlled by him whereby property is endangered or injured
suffers a fire upon his own land to escape beyond the limits thereof to the injury of another

266/10.plain: Setting fire to, attempting to burn, or helping burn an insured building or goods, wilfully and with intent to defraud or injure the insurer, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: sets fire to, or attempts to set fire to
causes to be burned
aids, counsels or procures the burning of, a building

266/11.plain: Within 24 hours before a fire, wilfully and without right disabling a nearby fire alarm system or damaging fire engines, hose or apparatus is punishable by up to 2 years of imprisonment or a $500 fine.
acts: cuts or removes a bell rope or a wire or conduit connected with a fire alarm signal system or injures or disables any fire alarm signal box or any part of such system in the vicinity of such building or property
cuts, injures or destroys an engine, hose or other fire apparatus in said vicinity

266/12.plain: During a fire, wilfully and maliciously disabling a fire alarm system, preventing an alarm, damaging fire apparatus, or obstructing putting out the fire is punishable by up to 7 years in state prison.
acts: cuts or removes a bell rope or a wire or conduit connected with a fire alarm signal system or injures or disables any fire alarm signal box or any part of such system in the vicinity of such building or property, or otherwise prevents an alarm being given
cuts, injures or destroys an engine, hose or other fire apparatus, in said vicinity, or otherwise wilfully and maliciously prevents or obstructs the extinction of a fire

266/13.plain: Wantonly or maliciously injuring a fire engine or other fire apparatus is punishable by up to 2 years of imprisonment or a $500 fine, plus a court-ordered good-behavior bond.
acts: injures a fire engine or other fire apparatus

266/13A.plain: A hotel manager, or whoever is in charge, who fails to notify the fire department of a fire and sound the required alarm when it threatens guest rooms can get up to 2½ years in jail.
acts: notify the fire department
sound the alarm system required by the state building code

266/14.plain: Breaking into a dwelling at night to commit a felony while someone is lawfully inside and the burglar is armed or assaults someone is punishable by up to life, with at least 10 years (15 if armed with a firearm).
acts: breaks and enters a dwelling house in the night time
after having entered with such intent, breaks such dwelling house in the night time

266/15.plain: Breaking into a dwelling at night with intent to commit a felony, without being armed or assaulting anyone, is punishable by up to 20 years in state prison, with at least 5 years for repeat offenders.
acts: breaks and enters a dwelling house in the night time
having entered with such intent, breaks such dwelling house in the night time

266/16.plain: Breaking into a building, ship or vehicle at night to commit a felony, or breaking or blowing open a safe or vault to commit larceny or a felony, is punishable by up to 20 years in state prison.
acts: breaks and enters a building, ship, vessel or vehicle
attempts to or does break, burn, blow up or otherwise injures or destroys a safe, vault or other depository of money, bonds or other valuables in any building, vehicle or place

266/16A.plain: Breaking and entering a building, ship, vessel or vehicle, day or night, with intent to commit a misdemeanor is punishable by up to 6 months of imprisonment, a $200 fine, or both.
acts: breaks and enters a building, ship, vessel or vehicle

266/17.plain: Entering a building, ship or vehicle at night without breaking, or breaking in by day, to commit a felony while putting someone inside in fear is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison; with a firearm, at least 7 years.
acts: enters without breaking, or breaks and enters in the day time, a building, ship, vessel, or vehicle
commits any offense described in this section while armed with a firearm

266/18.plain: Entering a dwelling at night without breaking, or breaking into a building, ship, vessel or motor vehicle by day, to commit a felony is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison; with a firearm, at least 7 years.
acts: enters a dwelling house without breaking, or breaks and enters in the day time a building, ship or motor vehicle or vessel
commits any offense described in this section while armed with a firearm

266/18A.plain: Entering a dwelling by false pretenses, without breaking, to commit a felony, or entering that way and then committing larceny, without putting anyone in fear, is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: enters a dwelling house by false pretenses, without breaking
after having entered, commits a larceny

266/19.plain: Breaking and entering a railroad car, or entering one at night without breaking, with intent to commit a felony is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: breaks and enters, or enters in the night time without breaking, a railroad car

266/20.plain: Stealing in a building, ship, vessel or railroad car is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: steals in a building, ship, vessel or railroad car

266/20A.plain: Breaking and entering, or entering without breaking, a truck, tractor-trailer, trailer, semi-trailer or freight container to commit a felony is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: breaks and enters, or enters without breaking, a truck, tractor/trailer unit, trailer, semi-trailer or freight container

266/20B.plain: Stealing in a truck, tractor-trailer, trailer, semi-trailer or freight container is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: steals in a truck, tractor/trailer unit, trailer, semi-trailer or freight container

266/21.plain: A person convicted of burglary, robbery, or related break-in crimes who keeps property taken in the crime and refuses the owner's request to return it can get up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: has in his possession or control money, goods, bonds or bank notes, or any paper of value, or any property of another
refuses or fails so to do while having power to deliver the same

266/22.plain: Breaking or entering, or entering at night without breaking, a building or enclosure holding live poultry to commit larceny is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison; the owner may detain the offender up to 24 hours.
acts: breaks or enters or enters in the night without breaking any building or enclosure wherein is kept or confined any kind of live poultry

266/23.plain: Stealing, carrying away or hiding belongings of people whose buildings are on fire or endangered, and not returning them or giving notice within two days, is larceny; the penalty is not set in this section.
acts: steals, conveys away or conceals any furniture, goods, chattels, merchandise or effects of persons whose houses or buildings are on fire or are endangered thereby
does not, within two days thereafter, restore the same or give notice of his possession thereof to the owner

266/24.plain: Stealing in a building that is on fire, or stealing property removed because of a fire alarm, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: steals in a building which is on fire
steals property which has been removed in consequence of an alarm caused by fire

266/25.plain: Larceny from the person (pickpocketing, purse-snatching) is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison; repeat thefts from people 65 or older carry at least 2 years.
acts: commits larceny by stealing from the person of a person sixty-five years or older
commits larceny by stealing from the person of another

266/27.plain: Stealing a contractor's, builder's or mechanic's tool from a building under construction or repair is punishable by up to 6 months of imprisonment, a $100 fine, or both.
acts: steals any tool belonging to any contractor, builder or mechanic from any building during the course of its construction, completion, alteration or repair

266/27A.plain: Removing or hiding an insured motor vehicle or trailer, or helping do so, with intent to defraud the insurer is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison, a $500-$5,000 fine, and restitution.
acts: removes or conceals a motor vehicle or trailer belonging to himself or another
aids or abets in such removal or concealment

266/92.plain: Wilfully making or publishing a false or exaggerated statement about a business's or person's finances or assets, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to 10 years in prison and a $5,000 fine.
acts: makes or publishes, or causes or permits to be made or published in any way whatever, any book, prospectus, notice, report, statement, exhibit, advertisement or other publication

266/92A.plain: Selling a motor vehicle without disclosing in writing on the bill of sale that it was flood-damaged or used as a police car, taxi, rental or leased vehicle, or selling a police car without removing its markings, is punishable by a fine of up to $500.
acts: sells a motor vehicle
sells any such police car to an ultimate user for other than police purposes without first having obliterated all evidence of distinctive police insignias or markings thereon

266/93.plain: Obtaining an animal breed registration by false pretence, or knowingly making or giving a false written pedigree of an animal, is punishable by up to 2 years in prison and a $500 fine.
acts: obtains from any club, association, society or company for improving the breed of cattle, horses, sheep, swine or other domestic animals, the registration, or a certificate thereof, of any animal in the herd register
makes, exhibits or gives a false pedigree in writing of any animal

266/94.plain: Wilfully and without right damaging or removing boundary monuments, milestones, guideboards, building signs, public lamps or railings, or traffic signs and signals is punishable by up to 6 months in prison and restitution.
acts: breaks down, injures, removes or destroys a monument erected for the purpose of designating the boundaries of a town or of a tract or lot of land, or a tree which has been marked for that purpose
so breaks down, injures, removes or destroys a milestone, mileboard or guideboard erected upon a public way or railroad
defaces or alters the inscription on any such stone or board
mars or defaces a building or signboard
extinguishes a light or breaks, destroys or removes a lamp, lamp post, railing or post erected on a bridge, sidewalk, public way, court or passage
defaces or otherwise injures, removes, interferes with or destroys any traffic regulating sign, light, signal, marking or device lawfully erected or placed under public authority on any public way

266/95.plain: Wilfully or maliciously damaging or removing a monument or marker for a historic place or event is punishable by up to 2 years in prison or a $1,000 fine, plus reimbursing the state for the damage.
acts: removes, displaces, destroys, defaces, mars or injures any monument, tablet or other device erected to mark an historic place or to commemorate an historic event

266/96.plain: Wilfully and without right defacing or damaging any state-owned building is punishable by up to 2 years in prison or a fine of $100 to $1,000, plus reimbursing the state for the damage.
acts: defaces, mars or injures the walls, wainscoting or any other part of any building belonging to the commonwealth, or the appurtenances thereof, by cutting, writing or otherwise

266/97.plain: Wilfully damaging a courthouse, jail, house of correction or other county building is punishable by up to 2 years in prison or a fine of $100 to $1,000, plus reimbursing the county.
acts: mars or injures the walls, wainscoting or any other part of a court house, jail or house of correction, or of any other building or room used for county business, or the appurtenances thereof, by cutting, writing or otherwise

266/98.plain: Wilfully or wantonly damaging a school, church, or other educational or religious building, its grounds or its property is punishable by up to 2 years in prison and a $1,000 fine.
acts: destroys, defaces, mars or injures a schoolhouse, church or other building erected or used for purposes of education or religious instruction, or for the general diffusion of knowledge

266/98A.plain: Wilfully or wantonly damaging playground equipment in a public park or playground is punishable by a fine of up to $1,000.
acts: destroys, defaces, mars or injures any playground apparatus or equipment located in a public park or playground

266/99.plain: Defines "library materials and property" and "library premises" for the library theft and damage sections.

266/99A.plain: Stealing library materials by concealing and removing them, wilfully not returning overdue items, borrowing with false ID or another's card, or destroying library records is a crime; the top penalty is 5 years in state prison.
acts: conceals on his person or among his belongings any library materials or property and removes said library materials or property
fail to return the same within thirty days from the date of such notice
giving of a false identification or fictitious name, address or place of employment
borrowing or attempting to borrow any library material or property by:
alteration or destruction of library ownership records, electronic or catalog records retained apart from or applied directly to the library materials or property

266/100.plain: Willfully, maliciously or wantonly damaging or destroying library materials or property is punishable by up to 2 years in a house of correction, a fine, and full restitution.
acts: writes upon, injures, defaces, tears, cuts, mutilates or destroys any library material or property

266/101.plain: Defines terms such as explosive, destructive or incendiary device, hoax device, and chemical, biological and nuclear weapon for the explosives and weapons sections that follow.

266/102.plain: Possessing ingredients to make a bomb or a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon, possessing an explosive or incendiary device, or using a hoax device to cause fear is a crime; the top penalty is 20 years in state prison.
acts: has in his possession or under his control:

has in his possession or uses or places, or causes another to knowingly or unknowingly possess, use or place, any hoax explosive, hoax destructive or incendiary device or substance or any hoax chemical, biological or nuclear weapon
has in his possession or under his control any explosive or any destructive or incendiary device or substance

266/102A.plain: Without lawful authority secreting, throwing, launching or placing an explosive or incendiary device to cause fear, to set it off, or to release a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon is punishable by up to 25 years in state prison.
acts: secretes, throws, launches or otherwise places an explosive or a destructive or incendiary device or substance

266/102B.plain: Without lawful authority willfully setting off or exploding a destructive or incendiary device or substance is punishable by 15 to 25 years in state prison, a $50,000 fine, or both.
acts: discharges, ignites or explodes any destructive or incendiary device or substance

266/102C.plain: Knowingly developing, producing, acquiring, possessing or using a biological, chemical or nuclear weapon or delivery system, with intent to cause death, injury or property damage, is punishable by up to 25 years in state prison.
acts: develops, produces, stockpiles, acquires, transports, possesses, controls, places, secretes or uses any biological, chemical or nuclear weapon or delivery system

266/102D.plain: Requires notice of seized explosives or weapons to the state fire marshal, forfeiture on conviction, and restitution to public agencies by people convicted of the explosives and weapons offenses.

266/103.plain: Wilfully throwing or placing acid, coal tar or other noxious or filthy substances on a house, building or vessel to damage or defile it is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: throws into, against or upon a dwelling house, office, shop or other building, or vessel, or puts or places therein or thereon oil of vitriol, coal tar or other noxious or filthy substance

266/104.plain: Wilfully and without right damaging or defacing a house or other building, inside or outside, is punishable by up to 2 months in prison or a $50 fine.
acts: destroys, injures, defaces or mars a dwelling house or other building, whether upon the inside or outside

266/104A.plain: Wilfully and without right destroying, damaging or removing a football goal post is punishable by a fine of $50 to $200.
acts: destroys, injures or removes a goal post on a football field

266/104B.plain: Entering an animal research facility and without authority damaging or removing its property or data, or releasing or interfering with its animals, is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison if malicious.
acts: enters any premises in which animals are being housed or used in research by a research institution
injures, damages, commits any trespass upon, removes or carries away any data, equipment, facility or property
injures, damages, removes, carries away, interferes with or releases any animal

266/105.plain: Wilfully and without right pulling down or removing part of a stone wall or fence that encloses land is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: pulls down or removes any portion of a stone wall or fence which is erected or maintained for the purpose of enclosing land

266/106.plain: Wilfully and without right damaging ice on waters where ice is harvested for sale, so that taking it is hindered or its value reduced, is punishable by a fine of up to $100.
acts: cuts, injures, mars or otherwise damages or destroys ice upon waters from which ice is or may be taken as an article of merchandise

266/107.plain: Wilfully and without right damaging or destroying a public bridge or a canal lock, culvert or embankment, or breaching a canal embankment, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: breaks down, injures, removes or destroys a public bridge, or a lock, culvert or embankment of a canal
makes an aperture or breach in such embankment

266/108.plain: Destroying a ship or vessel by casting it away, burning or sinking it, to injure or defraud its owner, cargo owner or insurer, is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison plus restitution.
acts: casts away, burns, sinks or otherwise destroys a ship or vessel

266/109.plain: Loading, equipping or fitting out a ship or vessel, or helping to, intending it be destroyed in order to injure or defraud its owner or insurer, is punishable by up to 20 years in state prison.
acts: lades, equips or fits out, or assists in lading, equipping or fitting out, a ship or vessel

266/110.plain: A ship or cargo owner, or someone involved in loading a vessel, who makes or shows a false invoice, bill of lading or other estimate of cargo to defraud an insurer faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: makes out or exhibits, or causes to be made out or exhibited, a false or fraudulent invoice, bill of lading, bill or parcels or other false estimates of any goods or property laden or pretended to be laden on board such ship or vessel

266/111.plain: A ship's master, officer or mariner who makes or swears to a false affidavit or protest, or an owner who procures or exhibits one, to defraud an insurer faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: makes or causes to be made or swears to a false affidavit or protest
procures such false affidavit or protest to be made, or exhibits the same

266/111A.plain: Presenting, or making or preparing for presentation, a document with a false or fraudulent material statement in support of an insurance claim, with intent to defraud the insurer, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: presents to it, or aids or abets in or procures the presentation to it of, any notice, statement, proof of loss, bill of lading, bill of parcels, invoice, schedule, account or other written document

makes, prepares or subscribes, or aids or abets in or procures the making, preparation or subscription of, any such notice, statement, proof of loss, bill of lading, bill of parcels, invoice, schedule, account or other written document

266/127B.plain: Gives anyone injured or whose property is damaged by violations of section 127A or section 39 of chapter 265 a civil action for injunctive relief, damages and attorney fees, and makes parents liable for judgments against their minor children.

266/128.plain: Defacing a milk dealer's name or mark on a milk can without the owner's consent, or using such a can in business with intent to defraud, is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: effaces, alters or covers over, or procures to be effaced, altered or covered over, the name, initial or device of any dealer in milk, marked or stamped upon a milk can
detains or uses in his business any such can having the name, initial or device of any dealer in milk so marked or stamped thereon

266/129.plain: An inmate of a state correctional institution who wilfully and maliciously destroys or injures property of the commonwealth there, or of anyone furnishing materials for prisoners' work, may get up to 3 years in state prison.
acts: destroys or injures the property of the commonwealth at such correctional institution, or the property of any person who furnishes materials for the employment of the prisoners

266/130.plain: A prisoner at a jail or house of correction who wilfully and maliciously injures or destroys public property or materials furnished for prisoners' work may be imprisoned for 6 months to 2½ years.
acts: injures or destroys any public property or any materials furnished for the employment of prisoners in such jail or house of correction

266/131.plain: Allows a person caught wilfully injuring a fruit or forest tree or committing malicious mischief on Sunday to be arrested without a warrant and held until a complaint is made, but not beyond the following day.

266/132.plain: Wilfully killing pigeons on, or frightening them from, beds made for netting them, within 100 rods, except on one's own land, is punishable by up to 1 month in prison or a $20 fine, plus damages.
acts: kills pigeons upon, or frightens them from, beds which have been made for the purpose of taking them in nets, by any method, within one hundred rods of the same

266/133.plain: Unlawfully entering a Humane Society house, boat house or hut and damaging or taking property, or damaging or trespassing on its life-saving property, is punishable by up to 6 months in prison or a $200 fine.
acts: unlawfully enters a house, boat house or hut which is the property of the Humane Society of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and wilfully injures, removes or carries away any property belonging to said society
injures or unlawfully uses or commits any trespass upon the property of said society which is intended or kept for the purpose of saving or preserving human life
commits any trespass upon such house, hut or boat house

266/135.plain: Mooring a vessel to a U.S. government buoy, beacon or floating guide in state waters is punishable by a fine of up to $50; wilfully destroying, injuring or removing one, by up to 3 months or a $100 fine.
acts: moors or in any manner makes fast a vessel, scow, boat or raft to a buoy, beacon or floating guide placed by the government of the United States in the navigable waters of the commonwealth
destroys, injures or removes any such beacon or guide

266/137.plain: Knowingly raising a river or stream by a dam so that it floods or injures a lawfully existing mill in the commonwealth, without right, is punishable by up to 6 months in prison or a $1,000 fine.
acts: causes the water of a river or stream so to be raised as to flow upon or injure a mill lawfully existing in the commonwealth and belonging to a citizen thereof

266/138.plain: Wilfully damaging a dam, reservoir, canal, mill gear or mill machinery, or wilfully or wantonly draining or blocking water in a mill pond or reservoir, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: breaks down, injures, removes or destroys a dam, reservoir, canal or trench, or a gate, flume, flashboards or other appurtenances thereof, or a wheel, or mill gear, or machinery of a water mill or steam mill
draws off the water contained in a mill pond, reservoir, canal or trench, or obstructs such water from flowing out of the same

266/138A.plain: Wilfully and without right damaging or disabling machinery or equipment used to carry water for agricultural purposes is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: damages or renders unusable machinery or equipment used in the transmission of water for agricultural purposes

266/139.plain: Removing or altering a motor vehicle or trailer's identifying numbers, or selling vehicles or parts knowing the numbers were altered, is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison; stealing another's registration plate, up to 2½ years.
acts: removes, defaces, alters, changes, destroys, obliterates or mutilates or causes to be removed or destroyed or in any way defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated, the identifying number or numbers of a motor vehicle or trailer
sells, transfers, distributes, dispenses or otherwise disposes of or attempts to sell, transfer, distribute, dispense or otherwise dispose of any motor vehicle or trailer or motor vehicle part
buys, receives, possesses, or obtains control of a motor vehicle, trailer, or motor vehicle part
takes and carries away the registration plate that is attached to the vehicle of another or is assigned by the registry of motor vehicles to another

266/139A.plain: Removing or altering the identifying numbers of any machine or electrical or mechanical device to conceal it, defraud, hinder competition or hide a crime, or selling such a device knowingly, is punishable by up to 1 year in jail.
acts: removes, defaces, alters, changes, destroys, obliterates or mutilates or causes to be removed or destroyed or in any way defaced, altered, changed, obliterated or mutilated, the identifying number or numbers of any machine or any electrical or mechanical device
sells or otherwise disposes of or attempts to sell or otherwise dispose of a machine or an electrical or a mechanical device

266/140.plain: Selling, offering to sell, or soliciting offers to buy a master key for more than one motor vehicle, knowing it will be used illegally, is punishable by up to 1 year in prison, a $500 fine, or both.
acts: sells or offers to sell or solicits offers to purchase a master key designed to fit more than one motor vehicle

266/141.plain: Makes anyone who uses odometer-altering devices, resets odometers, or knowingly drives with a disconnected odometer to defraud liable in a civil action for triple damages or $1,500, and treats it as unfair competition.

266/141A.plain: Turning back or readjusting a motor vehicle's speedometer or odometer to misrepresent its mileage to a buyer is punishable by a $500 to $1,000 fine, 30 days to 2 years in jail, or both.
acts: turns back or readjusts the speedometer or odometer thereof

266/142.plain: A business buying copper line wire or scrap copper wire that fails to record each purchase and seller in a book open to police inspection faces a fine of up to $50.
acts: violates any provision of this section

266/142A.plain: Gold, silver and platinum buyers must record purchases of $50 or more in a book open to police, and sellers must show photo ID; violations bring up to 1 year in prison, a $1,000 fine, or both.
acts: violates any provision of this section

266/143.plain: Defines "article" or "recorded device," "audiovisual recording function," "motion picture theater" and "owner" for sections 143A to 143H on unauthorized recordings.

266/143A.plain: Knowingly copying sound recordings without the owner's consent to sell, rent or use them for profit, or knowingly selling such copies, is a crime punished as provided in section 143E.
acts: transfers or causes to be transferred any sound recorded on a phonograph record, disc, wire, tape, film, videocassette or other article on which such sound is recorded
sells any such article

266/143B.plain: Recording a live performance without the owner's consent for commercial gain, or selling, renting or possessing such recordings knowing they were unauthorized, is a crime punished as provided in section 143E.
acts: records or causes to be recorded a live performance
advertises, sells, rents, transports or causes to be advertised, sold, rented or transported, or possesses for any of such purposes, a recording of a live performance

266/143C.plain: Knowingly making, renting, selling, transporting or possessing for sale recorded devices whose packaging lacks the true name and address of the transferor, for commercial gain, is punished as provided in section 143E.
acts: manufactures, rents, sells, transports, or causes to be manufactured, rented, sold or transported, or possesses for purposes of sale, rental or transport, any recorded device the outside packaging of which does not clearly and conspicuously bear the true name and address of the transferor of the sounds or images contained thereon

266/143D.plain: States that sections 143A to 143C do not apply to persons lawfully entitled to use the sounds or images, to radio or television broadcasts or archival preservation, or to law enforcement officers acting lawfully.

266/143E.plain: Sets penalties for violating sections 143A to 143C on unauthorized recordings: up to 1 year in a house of correction, rising to up to 5 years in state prison for 1,000 or more sound or 65 or more audiovisual recordings.
acts: violates any provision of section 143A to section 143C, inclusive

266/143F.plain: Knowingly operating a recording device in a movie theater during a showing to unlawfully record the film without consent is punishable by up to 2 years in a house of correction, or 5 years in state prison for repeat offenses.
acts: operates an audiovisual recording function

266/143G.plain: Gives a defense to false arrest or false imprisonment claims for reasonably detaining a person at a movie theater on reasonable grounds of a section 143F recording violation.

266/143H.plain: Allows the court, upon a conviction under sections 143A to 143C or 143F, to order forfeiture or destruction of the recordings and equipment used, stayed pending appeal.

266/144.plain: Carrying away or converting a stamped plastic or wire milk case or milk-products container without the owner's permission is punishable by a fine of $10 to $100.
acts: carries away or converts to his own use a plastic or wire milk case or a plastic or wire container for milk products which has been indelibly stamped with the name of a milk dealer or association of milk dealers

266/145.plain: Intentionally concealing a public record of the commonwealth or a local government, intending to permanently deprive it of the record, is punishable by a fine of up to $500.
acts: conceals upon his person or otherwise any record of the commonwealth or a political subdivision thereof

266/146.plain: Wilfully dumping solid waste in another's commercial disposal container without the owner's or custodian's consent is punishable by a fine of $100 to $1,000.
acts: deposits solid waste in a commercial disposal container of another

266/28.plain: Stealing, maliciously damaging, receiving or concealing a stolen motor vehicle or trailer is punishable by up to 15 years in state prison; concealing a vehicle thief carries up to 10 years.
acts: steals a motor vehicle or trailer
maliciously damages a motor vehicle or trailer
buys, receives, possesses, conceals, or obtains control of a motor vehicle or trailer
takes a motor vehicle without the authority of the owner and steals from it any of its parts or accessories
conceals any motor vehicle or trailer thief

266/29.plain: Requires the owner to report a stolen vehicle, sets police notice duties when it is recovered, and requires restitution to the insurer after a conviction under the motor vehicle theft section.

266/29B.plain: Requires the owner of record of a burned motor vehicle to submit a signed statement to the fire department.

266/30.plain: Larceny is stealing, or obtaining by false pretense or converting, another's property; it carries up to 5 years in state prison over $1,200 or for a firearm, and up to 10 years if the victim is 60 or older or disabled.
acts: steals
obtains by a false pretence
secretes
takes, carries away, conceals or copies
obtains by a false pretense

266/30A.plain: Shoplifting is intentionally taking, concealing or altering the price of store merchandise to deprive the merchant; under $250 it is a fine at first, and $250 or more carries up to 2½ years in the house of correction.
acts: takes possession of, carries away, transfers or causes to be carried away or transferred
conceals upon his person or otherwise
alters, transfers or removes any label, price tag or marking indicia of value
transfers any merchandise displayed, held, stored or offered for sale by any store or other retail mercantile establishment from the container
records a value for the merchandise which is less than the actual retail value
removes a shopping cart from the premises of a store or other retail mercantile establishment

266/30B.plain: Making, selling, possessing or using theft-detection shielding devices, or deactivators and removers, or deactivating or removing a theft detection device with intent to steal, carries up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: manufactures, sells, offers for sale or distributes a laminated or coated bag or other device intended to shield merchandise from detection by an electronic or magnetic theft detector
possesses a laminated or coated bag or device intended to shield merchandise from detection by an electronic or magnetic theft detector
possesses any tool or device designed or adapted to either:

manufacturers, sells, offers for sale or distributes a tool or device designed or adapted to allow the deactivation of a theft detection device or to allow the removal of a theft detection device from merchandise
deactivates or removes a theft detection device from merchandise prior to purchase, in a retail establishment

266/30C.plain: Possessing, using, making or counterfeiting retail receipts, price tickets or UPC labels to cheat a retailer is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: possesses, uses, utters, transfers, makes, alters, counterfeits or reproduces a retail sales or return receipt, price ticket or universal product code label

266/30D.plain: Organized retail crime, theft of over $2,500 in retail goods with 2 or more others to resell, carries up to 10 years; over $10,000, up to 15 years; leading such an enterprise, up to 20 years.
acts: steals, embezzles or obtains by fraud, false pretense or other illegal means retail merchandise valued at more than $2,500
steals, embezzles or obtains by fraud, false pretense or other illegal means retail merchandise valued at more than $10,000
conspires with others as an organizer, supervisor, financier or manager, to commit an organized retail crime or an aggravated organized retail crime

266/31.plain: Obtaining a person's signature on a written instrument by false pretense and with intent to defraud is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: obtains the signature of a person to a written instrument

266/32.plain: A ship captain who embezzles or fraudulently converts money, goods or property belonging to the crew, owners or suppliers of the vessel is guilty of larceny.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts or appropriates money, goods or property, held or possessed by or delivered to him

266/33.plain: Obtaining a note, release, extension of time, or contract change by false pretense, or bank credit by a false written financial statement, with intent to defraud, is larceny.
acts: obtains by a false pretence the making, acceptance or endorsement of a bill of exchange or promissory note, the release or substitution of collateral or other security, an extension of time for the payment of an obligation, or the release or alteration of the obligation of a written contract
obtains for himself or for any other person credit from any bank or trust company

266/33A.plain: Fraudulently obtaining, attempting to obtain, or helping another obtain a commercial computer service is punishable by up to 2½ years in a house of correction.
acts: obtains, or attempts to obtain, or aids or abets another in obtaining, any commercial computer service by false representation, false statement, unauthorized charging to the account of another, by installing or tampering with any facilities or equipment or by any other means

266/34.plain: Inducing another by false pretense and with intent to defraud to part with property, or with benefits described in the contract and computer-service fraud provisions, is larceny.
acts: induces another to part with property of any kind or with any of the benefits described in sections 33 and 33A

266/35.plain: Says the general larceny, signature and inducement sections do not apply to a purchase by false pretense about means to pay when payment is not due at delivery, unless the pretense is in a signed writing.

266/35A.plain: Making or using false material statements in the mortgage lending process, or receiving proceeds of such fraud, carries up to 5 years in state prison; a pattern across 3 or more properties carries up to 15 years.
acts: makes or causes to be made any material statement that is false or any statement that contains a material omission
uses, or facilitates the use of, any material statement that is false or any statement that contains a material omission
receives any proceeds or any other funds in connection with a residential mortgage closing
files or causes to be filed with a registrar of deeds any document that contains a material statement that is false or a material omission
engages in a pattern of residential mortgage fraud

266/37.plain: Making or passing a check with intent to defraud, knowing there are insufficient funds, is attempted larceny, and larceny if money, property or services are obtained.
acts: makes, draws, utters or delivers any check, draft or order for the payment of money upon any bank or other depositary

266/37A.plain: Defines terms such as credit card, cardholder, issuer, receives and falsely makes for the credit card misuse sections.

266/37B.plain: Misusing a credit card with intent to defraud, such as stealing, selling, forging a signature or using one for up to $1,200, is punishable by up to 1 year in jail or a $2,500 fine.
acts: makes or causes to be made, either directly or indirectly, any false statement as to a material fact in writing
takes a credit card from the person, possession, custody or control of another without the cardholder's consent by any conduct which would constitute larceny
receives the credit card
receives a credit card that he knows to have been lost, mislaid, or delivered under a mistake as to the identity or address of the cardholder
sells a credit card, or buys a credit card from a person other than the issuer or his authorized agent
signs a credit card

uses, for the purpose of obtaining money, goods, services or anything else of value, a credit card obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked

obtains money, goods, services or anything else of value by representing without the consent of the cardholder that he is said cardholder or by representing that he is the holder of a card and such card has not in fact been issued

furnishes money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of a credit card which he knows was obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked
fails to furnish money, goods, services or anything else of value which he represents in writing to the issuer that he has furnished
receives money, goods, services or anything else of value obtained in violation of clauses (f) to (i), inclusive
makes a false statement in reporting a credit card to be lost or stolen

266/37C.plain: Fraudulent credit card use over $1,200, false making or embossing of cards, and possessing incomplete cards or card-making equipment is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison or a $10,000 fine.
acts: obtains control over a credit card as security for debt
receives a credit card which he knows was taken or retained under circumstances which constitute credit card theft
falsely makes or falsely embosses a purported credit card or utters such a credit card

obtains money, goods, services or anything else of value by use of a credit card obtained or retained in violation of clauses (b) to (e), inclusive, of section thirty-seven B, or by use of a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked

obtains money, goods or services or anything else of value by representing without the consent of the cardholder that he is said cardholder or by representing that he is the holder of a card and such card has not in fact been issued

furnish money, goods, services or anything else of value upon presentation of a credit card which he knows was obtained in violation of subsections (b) to (e), inclusive, of section thirty-seven B, or a credit card which he knows is forged, expired or revoked
fails to furnish money, goods or services or anything else of value which he represents in writing to the issuer that he has furnished
receives money, goods, services or anything else of value obtained in violation of subsections (f) or (g) of section thirty-seven B
possesses one or more incomplete credit cards
machinery, plates or any other contrivance designed to reproduce instruments purporting to be the credit cards of an issuer who has not consented to the preparation of such credit cards

266/37D.plain: Publishing utility credit card numbers or coding systems, or methods to fraudulently avoid telecommunication payments, is punishable by up to 12 months in jail or a $2,000 fine.
acts: publishes or causes to be published the number or code of an existing, canceled, revoked, expired, or nonexistent credit card issued by a public utility company

266/37E.plain: Identity fraud, posing as another and using their personal identifying information, or obtaining or possessing tools to get it, is punishable by up to 2½ years in a house of correction or a $5,000 fine.
acts: poses as another person without the express authorization of that person and uses such person's personal identifying information to obtain or to attempt to obtain money, credit, goods, services, anything of value, any identification card or other evidence of such person's identity, or to harass another
obtains personal identifying information about another person without the express authorization of such person
possesses a tool, instrument or other article adapted, designed or commonly used for accessing a person's financial services account number or code

266/38.plain: A carrier who embezzles or fraudulently converts collect-on-delivery money contrary to the consignor's instructions is guilty of larceny, as is a member, officer or employee of a carrier who so disposes of it.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts to his own use
disposes of such money in whole or in part or any substitute therefor for his own use or for the use of said co-partnership or corporation

266/38A.plain: Using the proceeds of a mortgage-secured construction loan for anything other than paying labor and materials before they are paid in full is punishable by up to 1 year in jail or a $500 fine.
acts: applies the proceeds of such loan, or any part thereof, to any use other than payment for labor and/or materials as aforesaid

266/39.plain: Stealing, or fraudulently destroying, mutilating or concealing a will or other testamentary instrument is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: steals
destroys, mutilates or conceals a will, codicil or other testamentary instrument

266/40.plain: A person convicted of larceny a further time after a prior larceny conviction, or of three larcenies at one court sitting, is a common and notorious thief, punishable by up to 20 years in state prison.
acts: afterward commits a larceny or is accessory thereto before the fact
is convicted at the same sitting of the court, as principal or accessory before the fact, of three distinct larcenies

266/41.plain: A second conviction for stealing a bicycle worth over $10 is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: is convicted of a second offence of the larceny of a bicycle

266/42.plain: Larceny of paper or plates designed for bank bills, with intent to injure or defraud by passing them as true, is punishable by life or any term of years in state prison.
acts: commits larceny of a printed piece of paper or blank designed for issue by any incorporated bank or banking company in the United States as a bank bill, certificate or promissory note

266/43.plain: A printer or custodian who keeps bank-bill paper or blanks without the corporation's consent, intending to pass them as true, is punishable by life or any term of years in state prison.
acts: retains it in his possession without the knowledge and consent of the corporation for which it was printed

266/47.plain: Wrongfully removing the collar from a licensed, collared dog is punishable by up to 6 months in prison or a $100 fine.
acts: wrongfully removes the collar from a dog which is licensed and collared as provided in chapter one hundred and forty

266/48.plain: Requires an officer who arrests a person for robbery or larceny to secure the allegedly stolen property, and says it is restored to the owner after conviction.

266/49.plain: Making, mending or possessing tools designed for breaking into buildings or safes, or a master key for motor vehicles, with intent to use them for crime is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: makes or mends, or begins to make or mend
has in his possession, an engine, machine, tool or implement adapted and designed for cutting through, forcing or breaking open a building, room, vault, safe or other depository
has in his possession a master key designed to fit more than one motor vehicle

266/50.plain: A person employed in the commonwealth's treasury who commits a fraud or embezzlement there faces a fine of up to $2,000 or state prison for life or any term of years.
acts: commits a fraud or embezzlement therein

266/51.plain: A county, city or town officer who embezzles or fraudulently converts local government property faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts
fraudulently takes or secretes with intent so to do, effects or property which belong to or are in possession of said county, city or town

266/52.plain: A bank officer, director, trustee, agent or employee who fraudulently converts or takes and secretes bank or depositor money or securities is guilty of larceny from the bank, with up to 15 years in state prison; aiders also face this.
acts: fraudulently converts, or fraudulently takes and secretes with intent so to do, any bullion, money, note, bill or other security for money which belongs to and is in possession of such bank, or which belongs to any person and is deposited therein
knowingly aids, counsels or procures such larceny to be committed

266/53.plain: Sets evidence rules for prosecutions of bank and other embezzlement: a fraudulent taking through agreement with a bank officer counts as taking by the officer, items need not be identified, and acts within six months of the indictment date may be shown.

266/53A.plain: A bank officer or employee who wilfully misapplies bank property, issues unauthorized instruments, makes bad loans, or falsifies records, or anyone who aids or abets, faces up to 10 years in state prison and a $10,000 fine.
acts: wilfully misapplies otherwise than as described in section fifty-two or fifty-three, any of the moneys, funds, credits or other property of such bank
executes or issues a certificate of deposit, order or bill of exchange, or makes an acceptance, purporting to be executed, issued or made by such bank
assigns any note, bond, draft, bill of exchange, mortgage, judgment, decree or other property of such bank
loans the funds or credit of such bank to any individual, corporation, joint stock company, trust, association or partnership
knowingly receives or accepts for such bank any fictitious, valueless, inadequate or irresponsible obligation directly or as security or endorsement
certifies any check drawn upon such bank
resorts to any fictitious or colorable loan, transfer or device to avoid any provision of law relating to such bank
knowingly makes or causes to be made any false entry in any book, report or statement of such bank
knowingly aids or abets any violation of this section

266/54.plain: A bank officer or employee who receives or permits a deposit knowing the bank is insolvent faces up to 2½ years in prison or a fine of up to $5,000, or both.
acts: receives or permits the receipt of any deposit

266/55.plain: A bank liquidating agent, commissioner's employee, or court-appointed receiver who embezzles or misapplies property in their possession is guilty of larceny and faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts, or fraudulently takes and secretes with intent so to do, or wilfully misapplies, moneys, funds, credits or other property in his possession by virtue of his appointment or employment

266/56.plain: A broker or corporate broker-officer who embezzles or fraudulently converts money, stock or security entrusted with written investment directions faces up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts such money, stock or security, or any part thereof, or the proceeds or any part of the proceeds thereof

266/57.plain: A trustee, guardian, conservator, executor or administrator who embezzles or fraudulently converts property held for another or for a public or charitable purpose faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts or appropriates money, goods or property held or possessed by him for the use or benefit, either wholly or partially, of some other person or for a public or charitable purpose
otherwise fraudulently disposes of or destroys such property

266/58.plain: An officer, agent, clerk or servant of a voluntary association who embezzles or fraudulently converts its property is guilty of larceny.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts, or fraudulently takes or secretes with intent so to do, effects or property which belong to such association or society, or which have come to his possession or are under his care by virtue of his office or employment

266/59.plain: Embezzling or fraudulently converting property of the volunteer militia, a veterans post or another voluntary association is simple larceny, even if the person is a member.
acts: embezzles or fraudulently converts, or secretes with intent to embezzle or fraudulently convert, money, goods or property or any part thereof which has been delivered to him

266/60.plain: Buying, receiving or helping conceal stolen or embezzled property, or taking police-represented stolen property, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: buys, receives or aids in the concealment of stolen or embezzled property
buys, receives or aids in the concealment of property
obtains or exerts control over property in the custody of any law enforcement agency, or any individual acting on behalf of a law enforcement agency

266/60A.plain: Buying, receiving, concealing, selling or pledging a trade secret known to be stolen, unlawfully converted or taken is punishable by up to 5 years in prison.
acts: buys, receives, conceals, stores, barters, sells or disposes of any trade secret, or pledges or accepts as security for a loan any trade secret

266/60B.plain: Lets crimes under this chapter committed in different counties or court districts be charged and prosecuted in any court having jurisdiction of at least one of them, if they could otherwise be joined for trial.

266/61.plain: Provides that a person on a first conviction for receiving stolen property who shows the theft was simple larceny and makes full restitution cannot be imprisoned in state prison.

266/62.plain: Anyone convicted of receiving stolen property after a prior like conviction, or of three or more such acts at one sitting, is a common receiver of stolen goods, with up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: buying, receiving or aiding in the concealment of stolen or embezzled property

266/63.plain: Wilfully and mischievously taking or using someone's boat, non-motor vehicle or draught animal without consent is punishable by up to 6 months in prison or a $300 fine.
acts: takes or uses a boat or vehicle, other than a motor vehicle
takes, drives, rides or uses any draught animal which is the property of another

266/64.plain: Hiring a horse, carriage or vehicle and, with intent to cheat, lying about the distance or refusing to pay the lawful fare is punishable by up to 2 months in prison, a $20 fine, or both.
acts: hires a horse, carriage or other vehicle
makes to the owner or his agent, after the use of a horse, carriage or other vehicle, a false statement of the distance which he has actually traveled with such horse, carriage or other vehicle
refuses to pay for the use of a horse, carriage or other vehicle the lawful fare established therefor by any town

266/65.plain: A corporate officer, agent, clerk, servant or other person who issues or signs stock or securities beyond the authorized amount, or disposes of such stock to defraud, faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: issues or signs with intent to issue a certificate of stock in a corporation

issues, signs or endorses with intent to issue, a bond, note, bill or other obligation or security in the name of such corporation, beyond the amount authorized by law or limited by the legal votes of such corporation or its proper officers
negotiates, transfers or disposes of such certificate with intent to defraud

266/66.plain: A corporate officer, agent, clerk, servant or other person who fraudulently issues, transfers or signs a stock certificate for someone not entitled to it faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: fraudulently issues or transfers a certificate of the stock of a corporation to a person who is not entitled thereto
fraudulently signs such certificate, in blank or otherwise

266/67.plain: Making a false entry or omitting a true entry in business books, or omitting stock records, with intent to defraud is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: makes a false entry or omits to make a true entry in any book of such person, firm or corporation
omits to make a true record or entry thereof

266/67A.plain: Intentionally making false statements, concealing facts, or submitting false or misleading materials in procurement for a government body is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison and a $10,000 fine.
acts: makes a material statement that is false;
omits or conceals a material fact in a written statement;
submits or invites reliance on a material writing or recording that is false, forged, altered, or otherwise lacking in authenticity;
submits or invites reliance on a sample, specimen, map, photograph, boundary-mark, or other object that is misleading in a material respect; or
uses any trick, scheme, or device that is misleading in a material respect;

266/67B.plain: Making or presenting a claim against the state or a local government body knowing it is false, fictitious or fraudulent is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison and a $10,000 fine.
acts: makes or presents to any employee, department, agency or public instrumentality of the commonwealth, or of any political subdivision thereof, any claim upon or against any department, agency, or public instrumentality of the commonwealth, or any political subdivision thereof

266/67C.plain: Knowingly and wilfully making a false entry or omitting a true entry in certain capital-facility construction project records is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison and a $5,000 fine.
acts: makes, or knowingly and wilfully causes to be made, a false entry or omission of a true entry in any books, record or account

266/68.plain: Makes the books of a person, firm or corporation, to which the defendant had access or a right of access, admissible in evidence at trial for crimes under the three preceding sections.

266/69.plain: A non-member who wilfully wears or uses a registered society, association or labor union insignia to pose as a member faces up to one month in prison, a $20 fine, or both.
acts: wears or uses the insignia, ribbon, badge, rosette, button or emblem thereof

266/69A.plain: Knowingly and fraudulently displaying or using a labor organization's seal, trademark or insignia is punishable by a fine of up to $1,000.
acts: displays or otherwise uses, in any manner whatsoever, the seal, trademark or insignia of any labor organization

266/70.plain: A non-member without authority who wilfully wears or uses a listed veterans organization's insignia, or displays it on property to falsely claim occupancy, faces up to one month in prison, a $20 fine, or both.
acts: wears or uses the insignia, distinctive ribbons or membership rosette or button thereof
displays on his property or permits to be displayed thereon any such insignia, distinctive ribbon, membership rosette or button, or any sign or statement

266/71.plain: Wilfully getting a signature, money or property by false pretences for a pretended degree or membership in a fraternal organization is punishable by up to 1 year in prison or a $500 fine, or both.
acts: obtains the signature of any person to any written application
obtains any money or property for any alleged or pretended degree, or for any alleged or pretended membership

266/111B.plain: Knowingly presenting a false or fraudulent claim or proof of loss to a motor vehicle, theft or comprehensive insurer, with intent to defraud, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison plus restitution.
acts: knowingly presents to it, or aids or abets in or procures the presentation to it of, any notice, statement, or proof of loss

266/111C.plain: Knowingly acting as a runner, or using, hiring or directing one, to defraud an insured or insurance carrier is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: acts as a runner or uses, solicits, directs, hires or employs another to act as a runner

266/112.plain: Wilfully and maliciously killing, maiming or disfiguring another person's animal, or poisoning it, is punishable by up to 7 years in state prison, and up to 10 years for a repeat offense.
acts: kills, maims or disfigures any horse, cattle or other animal of another person
administers or exposes poison with intent that it shall be taken or swallowed by any such animal

266/113.plain: Wilfully cutting, taking or destroying timber, plants, stone, soil or similar things on another's land without the owner's license is punishable by up to six months in jail or a $500 fine.
acts: wilfully cuts down or destroys timber or wood standing or growing on the land of another
carries away any kind of timber or wood cut down or lying on such land
digs up or carries away stone, ore, gravel, clay, sand, turf or mould from such land
cuts down or carries away sedge, grass, hay or any kind of corn, standing, growing or being on such land
roots, nuts, berries, grapes or fruit of any kind or any plant there being
cuts or takes therefrom any ferns, flowers or shrubs
carries away from a wharf or landing place any goods in which he has no interest or property

266/114.plain: Wilfully and maliciously (or wantonly) breaking glass in another's building, damaging fences or gates, or severing produce from another's land is punishable by up to six months or a $500 fine.
acts: breaks glass in a building which is not his own
breaks down, injures, mars or defaces a fence belonging to or enclosing land which is not his own
throws down or opens a gate, bars or fence, and leaves the same down or open
severs from the freehold of another any produce thereof or anything attached thereto

266/115.plain: Wilfully and maliciously entering an orchard, nursery, garden or cranberry meadow and taking or destroying plants or fruit without consent is punishable by up to six months or a $500 fine.
acts: enters an orchard, nursery, garden or cranberry meadow, and takes away, mutilates or destroys a tree, shrub or vine, or steals, takes and carries away any fruit or flower

266/116A.plain: Pulling up, digging up or injuring wild azalea, wild orchid or cardinal flower plants in public places or on another's land without written authority, or buying or selling them, is punishable by a fine of up to $5.
acts: pull up or dig up the plant of a wild azalea, wild orchid or cardinal flower (lobelia cardinalis), or any part thereof
injure any such plant or any part thereof
buy or sell, or offer or expose for sale, any such flower, or the whole or any part of the plant thereof

266/117.plain: Wilfully and intentionally entering another's orchard, garden or improved land without right, intending to cut, take or destroy plants or produce, is punishable by up to six months or a $500 fine.
acts: enters upon the orchard, garden or other improved land of another

266/118.plain: Wilfully letting sheep, goats, cattle, horses, swine or fowl in your charge stay on or cross another's improved land after written or posted notice is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: suffers or permits them to enter or remain on or pass over any orchard, garden, mowing land or other improved or enclosed land of another

266/119.plain: Knowingly bringing a regulated pest into the commonwealth, moving it between towns, or evading a quarantine regulation is punishable by a fine of up to $200, up to two months in jail, or both.
acts: brings into the commonwealth, or transports from one town to another therein, any pest referred to in section eleven or twenty-five of chapter one hundred and thirty-two, or the eggs, nests, larvae or pupae thereof
evades the requirements of a quarantine regulation duly established under any provision of said chapter one hundred and thirty-two

266/120.plain: Entering or remaining on another's building or land, or in a school bus, after being forbidden, or violating a related court order, is punishable by a fine of up to $100 or up to 30 days in jail.
acts: enters or remains in or upon the dwelling house, buildings, boats or improved or enclosed land, wharf, or pier of another
enters or remains in a school bus, as defined in section 1 of chapter 90

266/120A.plain: Provides that, in a prosecution for trespass by parking a motor vehicle on a private way or enclosed land, proof that the defendant was the registered owner is prima facie evidence the defendant parked it.

266/120B.plain: Provides that an abutting landowner who enters adjoining land to maintain or repair a building is not guilty of trespass or civilly liable if notice, bond and other conditions are met.

266/120C.plain: Provides that a registered land surveyor entering adjoining lands after reasonable notice to make surveys for a private person is not trespassing, but remains liable for damage caused.

266/120D.plain: Removing a vehicle from a private way or property without notifying police or the owner's consent, or purporting to authorize such removal without complying, is punishable by a fine of up to $100.
acts: removes a vehicle from a private way or from improved or enclosed property as aforesaid
purports to authorize the removal of a vehicle from a way or property as aforesaid without having fully complied with the provision of this section

266/120E.plain: Knowingly obstructing entry to or departure from a medical facility, or entering or remaining so as to impede services, after notice is punishable by up to six months in jail, and up to 2½ years for repeat violations.
acts: knowingly obstructs entry to or departure from any medical facility
enters or remains in any medical facility so as to impede the provision of medical services

266/120E1~2.plain: Defying a police withdrawal order at a reproductive health care facility, or injuring, intimidating, impeding or interfering with people or vehicles there, is punishable by fines or jail, up to 5 years in state prison for some repeat offenses.
acts: fails to comply with a withdrawal order pursuant to subsection (b)
intentionally injures or intimidates or attempts to injure or intimidate a person who attempts to access or depart from a reproductive health care facility
impedes a person's access to or departure from a reproductive health care facility
impedes or attempts to impede a person or a vehicle attempting to access or depart from a reproductive health care facility
interferes with the operation of a vehicle that attempts to enter, exit or park at a reproductive health care facility

266/120F.plain: Knowingly accessing a computer system without authorization, or staying in after learning access is unauthorized, is punishable by up to 30 days in a house of correction or a fine of up to $1,000.
acts: accesses a computer system by any means
fails to terminate such access

266/121.plain: Entering another's land without right with firearms intending to fire them, and staying after being asked to leave, is punishable by a fine of up to $200, up to two months in jail, or both.
acts: enters upon the land of another with firearms

266/121A.plain: Entering another's private land without right with a motor-powered vehicle, machine or device is punishable by a fine of up to $500.
