acts: enters upon the private land of another, whether or not such land be posted against trespass

266/122.plain: Wilfully tearing down, removing or defacing a posted no-trespassing notice is punishable by a fine of up to $25.
acts: tears down, removes or defaces any notice posted on land, or other property described in section one hundred and twenty, by the owner, lessee or custodian thereof, warning persons not to trespass thereon

266/123.plain: Willfully trespassing on state land or on listed public institution grounds, or staying after notice to leave, is punishable by a fine of up to $50 or up to three months in jail.
acts: trespasses upon land or premises belonging to the commonwealth
remains thereon

266/123A.plain: Willfully trespassing on public water sources or supply facilities after being forbidden is fined $250 to $1,000; doing so intending to pollute carries up to 5 years in state prison, and up to 10 years for repeats.
acts: trespasses upon any public source of water or public water supply facilities or land
commits any offense described in subsection (a)

266/124.plain: Wilfully and maliciously (or wantonly and without cause) tearing down or defacing a lawfully posted town meeting warrant, juror list or notice is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: tears down, removes or defaces a warrant for a town meeting, list of jurors or other notice or paper which has been posted in compliance with law

266/125.plain: Wilfully and maliciously removing, destroying or mutilating a posted show bill or advertisement for a licensed exhibition before it takes place is punishable by a fine of up to $10.
acts: removes, destroys or mutilates a show bill, placard, program or other advertisement posted upon a wall, fence, billboard or structure not lawfully under his control

266/126.plain: Painting or affixing unauthorized words, ads or notices on public or another's property without written consent is punishable by a fine of $10 to $100, plus forfeiture of removal costs.
acts: paints, or puts upon, or in any manner affixes to, any fence, structure, pole, rock or other object which is public property or the property of another

266/126A.plain: Intentionally, willfully and maliciously (or wantonly) defacing or destroying another's property is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison or 2 years in a house of correction, a fine, and paying for cleanup.
acts: paints, marks, scratches, etches or otherwise marks, injures, mars, defaces or destroys the real or personal property of another

266/126B.plain: Tagging by spraying paint or placing a sticker on property, alone or with a group, with intent to deface or damage it, is punishable by up to 2 years in a house of correction, a fine, and cleanup costs.
acts: sprays or applies paint or places a sticker upon a building, wall, fence, sign, tablet, gravestone, monument or other object or thing on a public way or adjoined to it, or in public view, or on private property

266/127.plain: Willfully and maliciously destroying or injuring another's personal property, dwelling or building in a way not described elsewhere in this chapter is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison; wanton damage by up to 2½ years.
acts: destroys or injures the personal property, dwelling house or building of another in any manner or by any means not particularly described or mentioned in this chapter

266/127A.plain: Willfully (or wantonly) destroying or defacing a church, burial place, school or community center, or threatening to destroy a place of worship, is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison for damage over $5,000.
acts: destroys, defaces, mars, or injures a church, synagogue or other building, structure or place used for the purpose of burial or memorializing the dead
threatens to burn, deface, mar, injure, or in any way destroy a church, synagogue or other building, structure, or place of worship

268/1.plain: Lying under oath in a court proceeding or where an oath is required is perjury, punishable by up to 20 years in state prison, or life or any term of years if committed at a capital trial.
acts: swears or affirms falsely in a matter material to the issue or point in question
swears or affirms falsely in a matter relative to which such oath or affirmation is required

268/1A.plain: Signing a written statement that carries a declaration it is made under the penalties of perjury, when it is wilfully false in a material matter, is perjury and carries perjury's penalties.
acts: signs and issues such a written statement containing or verified by such a written declaration

268/2.plain: Procuring another person to commit perjury (subornation of perjury) is punished the same as perjury.
acts: procuring another person to commit perjury

268/3.plain: Attempting to incite or procure another person to commit perjury is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison or up to 1 year in jail, even if no perjury is committed.
acts: attempts to incite or procure another person to commit perjury

268/4.plain: Lets a court of record commit a witness or require a recognizance when testimony creates a reasonable presumption of perjury, bind over witnesses to the superior court, and notify the district attorney.

268/5.plain: Lets a court detain papers, books or documents produced in a proceeding where perjury is presumed, for as long as needed for the perjury prosecution.

268/6.plain: Willfully making false reports to, or testifying falsely before, certain state departments, or falsely entering company books reported to them, is punishable by up to 1 year in prison and a $1,000 fine.
acts: make false report
testify or affirm falsely to any material fact in any matter wherein an oath or affirmation is required or authorized
make any false entry or memorandum upon any book, report, paper or statement of any company making report to any of the said departments or board or said commissioner
aids or abets another in any violation of this section

268/6A.plain: A public officer or employee who files or publishes a written report or statement known to be materially false in the course of official duties faces up to 1 year in prison and a $1,000 fine.
acts: executes, files or publishes any false written report, minutes or statement

268/6B.plain: A process server who willfully falsifies that service, or a particular kind of service, was made on a writ or other process returned to court faces up to 1 year in prison or a $500 fine.
acts: returns to the court a writ or other official instrument of process on which he has willfully falsified either the fact that service has been made, or the fact that a particular kind of service has been made

268/8B.plain: An appointing authority who compels or induces, by threats or coercion, a person on a civil service eligible list to refuse an appointment or promotion faces a fine and up to 2 months in jail.
acts: compels, or induces by the use of threats or other form of coercion, any person on an eligible list, as defined in chapter thirty-one, to refuse an appointment or promotion

268/9A.plain: Selling tickets to, or soliciting or accepting contributions for, a testimonial dinner for a law enforcement, regulatory or investigatory official (other than an elected one) is punishable by a fine of up to $500.
acts: sell, offer for sale, or accept payment for, tickets or admissions to, nor solicit or accept contributions for, a testimonial dinner or function

268/13.plain: Corrupting or trying to corrupt a master, auditor, juror, arbitrator, umpire or referee with a gift or promise to influence a decision is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: corrupts or attempts to corrupt a master in chancery, master, auditor, juror, arbitrator, umpire or referee by giving, offering or promising any gift or gratuity whatever

268/13A.plain: Picketing or parading near a court, or near a building or residence of a judge, juror, witness or court officer, to interfere with justice or influence them is punishable by up to 1 year and a $5,000 fine.
acts: pickets or parades in or near a building housing a court of the commonwealth, or in or near a building or residence occupied or used by such judge, juror, witness, or court officer

268/13B.plain: Willfully threatening, bribing, misleading, intimidating or harassing a witness, juror, or other person tied to a criminal case, to interfere with or retaliate over a proceeding, carries up to 10 years, or 20 in life-offense cases.
acts: threatens, attempts or causes physical, emotional or economic injury or property damage to
conveys a gift, offer or promise of anything of value to
misleads, intimidates or harasses another person

268/13C.plain: Causing or actively taking part in the willful disruption of a court's proceedings may be punished by a fine of up to $1,000, up to 1 year in jail or house of correction, or both.
acts: causes or actively participates in the willful disruption of proceedings of any court of the commonwealth

268/13D.plain: Knowingly distributing grand jury testimony transcripts or descriptions to interfere with a criminal proceeding or witness is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison or a $5,000 fine.
acts: distributes or possesses with intent to distribute any transcript of grand jury testimony or any substantially verbatim description of grand jury testimony

268/13E.plain: Altering, destroying, mutilating or concealing a record or object to impair its use in an official proceeding is punishable by up to 5 years, or up to 10 years if the proceeding involves a criminal statute violation.
acts: alters, destroys, mutilates, or conceals a record, document, or other object, or attempts to do so

268/14.plain: A juror, arbitrator, umpire, referee, master or auditor who corruptly takes anything to give a verdict or receives a gift from a party faces up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: takes anything to give his verdict, award or report
receives any gift or gratuity from a party to a suit, cause or proceeding

268/14A.plain: Forbids discharging or depriving a person of employment because of grand or traverse jury service; an employer who does so is in contempt of court.

268/14B.plain: An employer who fires or penalizes, or threatens to, an employee for missing work to be a witness or victim at a criminal action faces up to 1 month in prison or a $200 fine.
acts: subject an employee to discharge or penalty or the threat of discharge or penalty on account of the absence of such employee from employment by reason of his attendance as a witness at a criminal action

268/15.plain: Conveying escape tools into a jail or prison, helping a prisoner escape, or rescuing a prisoner is punishable by up to 10 years in state prison, depending on the prisoner's status.
acts: conveys into a correctional institution of the commonwealth or into a jail, house of correction, house of reformation or like place of confinement, a disguise, instrument, tool, weapon or other thing which is adapted or useful to aid a prisoner in making his escape
aids or assists such prisoner in endeavoring to escape therefrom
forcibly or fraudulently rescues or attempts to rescue a prisoner held in custody upon a conviction or charge of crime

268/15A.plain: Escaping from a city or town jail after being lawfully placed in custody is punishable by up to 2½ years in jail or house of correction, a $500 fine, or both.
acts: escapes from any such jail

268/16.plain: A prisoner who escapes or tries to escape, defeats electronic monitoring, or fails to return from temporary release faces up to 10 years in state prison.
acts: escapes or attempts to escape from any such institution or from land appurtenant thereto, or from any courthouse or from land appurtenant thereto or from the custody of any officer thereof while being conveyed to or from said institution, center or branch
disables or attempts to disable or defeat electronic monitoring of the prisoner
fails to return from any temporary release from said institution under the provisions of section ninety A of chapter one hundred and twenty-seven
fails to return from any temporary release from said institution, center or branch

268/17.plain: Aiding a prisoner to escape or attempt to escape from an officer or person with lawful custody is punishable by up to 2 years in prison or a $500 fine.
acts: aids or assists a prisoner in escaping or attempting to escape from an officer or person who has the lawful custody of such prisoner

268/18.plain: A jailer or officer who voluntarily lets a prisoner in custody escape suffers the same punishment the prisoner was sentenced to or would face for the charged crime.
acts: suffers a prisoner in his custody upon conviction or upon a charge of crime to escape

268/19.plain: A penal institution employee who voluntarily lets a convict escape, or consents to the escape, faces up to 20 years in state prison.
acts: suffers a convict confined therein to escape, or in any way consents to such escape

268/20.plain: A jailer or officer who negligently lets a prisoner escape, or wilfully refuses to receive a lawfully committed prisoner, faces up to 2 years in prison or a $500 fine.
acts: suffers a prisoner in his custody upon conviction or upon a charge of crime to escape
refuses to receive into his custody a prisoner lawfully directed to be committed thereto upon conviction, upon a charge of crime, or upon a lawful process

268/21.plain: A state prison employee who lets a convict be at large, or be visited or comforted contrary to prison regulations, faces a fine of up to $500.
acts: suffers a convict under sentence of solitary imprisonment to be at large or out of the cell assigned to him
suffers any convict confined in the prison to be at large out of the prison
to be visited, conversed with or in any way relieved or comforted

268/21A.plain: A correctional officer or contractor who has sexual relations with an inmate faces up to 5 years in state prison or a $10,000 fine, and the inmate is deemed unable to consent.
acts: engages in sexual relations with an inmate confined therein, within or outside of such institution, or an inmate who is otherwise under the direct custodial supervision and control of such officer or other person

268/22.plain: An officer who wilfully delays serving an arrest warrant or search warrant faces a fine of up to $50.
acts: delays service of a warrant of arrest or a search warrant committed to him for service

268/23.plain: An officer who wilfully and corruptly refuses or delays to execute process to apprehend or confine a person, so that the person escapes, faces a fine up to $500 or up to one year in prison.
acts: refuses to execute a lawful process directed to him and requiring him to apprehend or confine a person convicted of or charged with crime
omits or delays to execute such process

268/24.plain: Refusing or neglecting to help a sheriff, constable, police officer or watchman who requires it in a criminal case or to keep the peace is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to one month in prison.
acts: neglects or refuses to assist him in the execution of his office in a criminal case, in the preservation of the peace or in the apprehension or securing of a person for a breach of the peace, or in a case of escape or rescue of persons arrested upon civil process

268/25.plain: Refusing or neglecting to obey a justice of the peace who requires you to apprehend an offender is punished as set in the preceding section; ignorance of the justice's office is no excuse.
acts: refuses or neglects to obey such justice

268/26.plain: Giving, selling or delivering alcoholic beverages to a prisoner, or possessing them at a prison to deliver to a prisoner, is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to two months in prison.
acts: gives, sells or delivers alcoholic beverages, as defined in section one of chapter one hundred and thirty-eight, to a person confined in any correctional institution or other place of confinement, or to a person in the custody of a sheriff, constable, police officer, superintendent of a correctional institution, or other superintendent or keeper of a place of confinement
has in his possession, within the precincts of any prison or other place of confinement, any such beverages

268/27.plain: Giving, selling or delivering alcoholic beverages to a patient or inmate of a public institution, or possessing them there to consume or pass on, is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to two months in prison.
acts: gives, sells or delivers any alcoholic beverages, as defined in section one of chapter one hundred and thirty-eight, to any patient or inmate of any public institution, or to any patient or inmate under the control of any such institution
has in his possession within the precincts of any such institution any such beverages

268/28.plain: Giving or delivering any drug or article to a prisoner, or possessing one at a prison to give to a prisoner, without permission is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: gives or delivers to a prisoner in any correctional institution, or in any jail or house of correction, any drug or article whatever
has in his possession within the precincts of any prison herein named

268/29.plain: A sheriff, jailer or correctional officer who gives or permits alcohol to a prisoner, or keeps prisoners of different sexes or classes together, forfeits $25 or $50 and is removed from office on a second conviction.
acts: gives, sells or delivers or knowingly permits to be given, sold or delivered to a prisoner in his custody any alcoholic beverages
willingly or negligently suffers such prisoner to have or drink any alcoholic beverages
places or keeps together prisoners in his custody of different sexes or classes

268/30.plain: Wilfully disturbing a correctional institution or jail, or trying to attract the attention of or communicating with an inmate without permission, is punishable by a fine up to $50 or up to three months in prison.
acts: wilfully disturbs any correctional institution of the commonwealth
seeks to attract the attention of, or without the permission of the officer in charge has communication with, an inmate thereof

268/31.plain: Delivering or hiding articles for inmates, or taking articles from inmates, against institution rules is punishable by up to 3 years in state prison; an inmate bringing in drugs or weapons from furlough gets an added 7 to 10 years.
acts: delivers or procures to be delivered, or has in his possession with intent to deliver, to an inmate confined in any penal institution

deposits or conceals in or about the institution, or the dependencies thereof, or upon any land appurtenant thereto, or in any boat or vehicle going into the premises belonging to the institution, any article
receives from an inmate any article
brings or attempts to bring into said institution an illegal drug, gun, knife or other similar weapon

268/32.plain: Opening, tampering with or damaging a police or fire signal box, or a highway emergency call box, is punishable by up to 2 years in prison for police and fire boxes, or a fine for call boxes.
acts: opens a signal box connected with a police signal system
interferes in any way with such box by breaking, cutting, injuring or defacing the same
opens, tampers or meddles with such box, or with any part or parts thereof, or with the police signal wires, or with anything connected therewith
tampers or meddles with a signal box connected with a fire signal system or with any part or thing connected therewith
opens a motorist highway emergency aid call box on any state highway connected with a highway emergency signal system
opens, tampers or meddles with such box, or with any part or parts thereof, or with anything connected therewith
tampers or meddles with a motorist highway emergency aid call box or with any part or thing connected therewith

268/32A.plain: Willfully obstructing, interfering with or hindering a fire fighter or fire fighting force in the lawful performance of duty is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison.
acts: obstructs, interferes with or hinders a fire fighter in the lawful performance of his duty
obstructs, interferes with or hinders a fire fighting force in the lawful performance of its duty

268/32B.plain: Knowingly preventing or trying to prevent a police officer from making an arrest by force, threats, or other means creating a substantial risk of bodily injury is punishable by up to 2½ years in a house of correction.
acts: prevents or attempts to prevent a police officer, acting under color of his official authority, from effecting an arrest of the actor or another
using or threatening to use physical force or violence against the police officer or another
using any other means which creates a substantial risk of causing bodily injury to such police officer or another

268/33.plain: Falsely pretending to be a justice of the peace, notary, sheriff, police officer or other listed official or federal officer, and acting as one or demanding aid, is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to 2½ years in prison.
acts: falsely assumes or pretends to be a justice of the peace, notary public, sheriff, deputy sheriff, medical examiner, associate medical examiner, constable, police officer, probation officer, or examiner, investigator or other officer appointed by the registrar of motor vehicles, or inspector, investigator or examiner of the department of public utilities or the department of telecommunications and cable, or investigator or other officer of the alcoholic beverages control commission, or investigator or other official of the bureau of special investigations, or examiner, investigator or other officer of the department of revenue or an officer or employee acting under the authority of the United States or any department, agency or officer thereof

268/33A.plain: Conducting a lead paint inspection without a license, or falsely holding yourself out as a licensed inspector, is punishable by a fine up to $5,000, up to one year in jail, or both.
acts: engages in or conducts a lead paint inspection without being licensed to do so
holds himself out to the public as a licensed lead paint inspector and is not so licensed

268/34.plain: Wearing a disguise with intent to obstruct the law or to intimidate or hinder an officer or person in lawful duties or rights is punishable by a fine up to $500 or up to one year in prison.
acts: disguises himself

268/34A.plain: Knowingly and willfully giving a false name or other identifying information to a law enforcement officer after an arrest is punishable by a fine up to $1,000 or up to one year in a house of correction.
acts: furnishes a false name, Social Security number, date of birth, home address, mailing address or phone number, or other information as may be requested for the purposes of establishing the person's identity, to a law enforcement officer or law enforcement official following an arrest

268/35.plain: Without authority, using a town seal to make something look official, or making or possessing a badge like a town officer's with intent to assume an official character, is punishable by a fine up to $50.
acts: prints, stamps, engraves or affixes, or causes to be printed, stamped, engraved or affixed to any paper or other article a representation of the seal of a town in the commonwealth

casts, stamps, engraves, makes or has in his possession a badge or thing in the likeness of an official badge of a police officer, member of a fire department, or other officer appointed by a town in the commonwealth, or by any department of such town

268/36.plain: Taking money or a reward under an agreement to conceal a felony or not prosecute or give evidence is punishable by up to 5 years in state prison if the felony carries death or life, otherwise up to 2 years in jail.
acts: takes money, or a gratuity or reward, or an engagement therefor, upon an agreement or understanding, express or implied, to compound or conceal such felony, or not to prosecute therefor, or not to give evidence thereof

268/39.plain: Knowingly making a false written statement under penalty of perjury to police or the registry alleging a motor vehicle theft is punishable by up to 2 years, or 1 to 5 years for a repeat offense.
acts: makes a false written statement on a form bearing notice that false statements made therein are punishable under the penalty of perjury, to a police officer, police department or the registry of motor vehicles alleging the theft or conversion of a motor vehicle

268/40.plain: A person who knows another is a victim of rape, murder, manslaughter or armed robbery and is at the scene must report it to law enforcement when safe, or face a fine of $500 to $2,500.
acts: report said crime to an appropriate law enforcement official as soon as reasonably practicable
